t:
(a) Requirements for Restructuring Certification.—The Oversight Board, prior to issuing a restructuring certification regarding an entity (as such term is defined in section 101 of title 11, United States Code), shall determine, in its sole discretion, that—
        (1) the entity has made good-faith efforts to reach a consensual restructuring with creditors; 
        (2) the entity has—
            (A) adopted procedures necessary to deliver timely audited financial statements; and 
            (B) made public draft financial statements and other information sufficient for any interested person to make an informed decision with respect to a possible restructuring;  
        (3) the entity is either a covered territory that has adopted a Fiscal Plan certified by the Oversight Board, a covered territorial instrumentality that is subject to a Territory Fiscal Plan 
certified by the Oversight Board, or a covered territorial instrumentality that has adopted an Instrumentality Fiscal Plan certified by the Oversight Board; and 
        (4)
            (A) no order approving a Qualifying Modification under section 601 has been entered with respect to such entity; or 
            (B) if an order approving a Qualifying Modification has been entered with respect to such entity, the entity is unable to make its debt payments notwithstanding the approved Qualifying Modification, in which case, all claims affected by the Qualifying Modification shall be subject to a title III case.   
    (b) Issuance of Restructuring Certification.—The issuance of a restructuring certification under this section requires a vote of no fewer than 5 members of the Oversight Board in the affirmative, which shall satisfy the requirement set forth in section 302(2) of this Act.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the references to creditors and to making draft financial statements public for "any interested person" amount to outside participation. Those are conditions the debtor entity must already have met, not a process in which the decision-maker consults outsiders, takes comment, or holds a hearing. The Board decides "in its sole discretion" by an internal vote of its own members, and nothing in the section grants an outside party a right to sue or object.

opus.w: The Oversight Board decides the certification 'in its sole discretion' and by an internal vote of its members. It is never required to consult creditors, the public, or other outside parties. The mention of creditors and 'interested persons' describes things the debtor entity must already have done (negotiating with creditors, publishing financial statements), not a process where outsiders take part in the Board's decision. The tempting reading treats those creditor negotiations as participation, but they happen between the debtor and its creditors, not between the decision-maker and the public.

opus.b:
I'm labelling this **No**, with moderate confidence (0.68).

**The tempting reading.** Before the Oversight Board issues a restructuring certification, it must find that "the entity has made good-faith efforts to reach a consensual restructuring with creditors". It must also find that the entity has published draft financial statements "sufficient for any interested person to make an informed decision". Creditors and the public are outside parties, so this can look like participation.

**Why it fails.** Both duties fall on the debtor territory or its instrumentality, not on the decision-maker. The Board decides "in its sole discretion" and does not have to consult anyone. The only process is an internal vote of its own members. There is also some background (not in the text itself): under PROMESA, the Act this section comes from, the Board is placed within the territorial government, not the federal government. So it is doubtful this is a federal decision at all. The case for "Yes" is that a debtor's talks with its creditors are a precondition to the decision, which is why I'm not more certain.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Oversight Board to make a determination based on specific criteria, including whether the entity has made certain information public. While the information is made public for interested persons, the statute does not require the Board to consult with, coordinate with, or receive input from those interested persons or the general public before issuing the certification. The decision is made by the Board in its 'sole discretion' based on the entity's compliance with procedural requirements, not through a participatory process with outsiders.

(B) made public draft financial statements and other information sufficient for any interested person to make an informed decision with respect to a possible restructuring
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the entity must make "public draft financial statements... for any interested person to make an informed decision," this constitutes public participation. However, this is a disclosure requirement imposed on the entity (likely a government instrumentality) to ensure transparency, not a mechanism for the public to consult with or advise the federal Oversight Board before it makes its decision. The Oversight Board's decision is based on its own determination of the entity's compliance with specific criteria, not on public input.
